html:
The Nongatl were an Athabaskan-speaking people of northwestern California, living in the hills along the Van Duzen River and the upper Mad and Eel rivers, in Humboldt and Trinity counties. They are one of the Eel River Athabaskan groups, with the Wailaki, Lassik and Sinkyone, related in language to the Athabaskan peoples of the far north.

They lived in small villages, gathering acorns and catching salmon. In the 1850s and 1860s American settlers and militias killed most of the Eel River peoples, and very few Nongatl survived. Their descendants are part of other tribes and rancherias of the region. See also California genocide.
